html:
John the Cappadocian was the praetorian prefect of the East, the chief finance and tax minister of Justinian I, from 531 to 541. He rose from a clerk's post and was known for raising money without mercy.

His taxes and squeezing of officials made him hated, and the rioters of the Nika riots in 532 demanded his dismissal. Justinian gave in, then brought him back within months. He was needed: the emperor was paying for the war against the Vandals and the later Gothic War. John cut costs and trimmed the imperial post, the state courier service. The historian Procopius says he did it by cruelty and corruption, though Procopius disliked him.

His end came through palace politics. Theodora resented him, and in 541 Belisarius's wife Antonina and John's own daughter Euphemia drew him into talk of seizing power, while Theodora's agents listened. He lost his post and his wealth, was made a priest and was sent away, first to Cyzicus and then to Egypt. He is said to have returned after Theodora's death in 548.
sum: John the Cappadocian was the praetorian prefect of the East, the chief finance and tax minister of Justinian I, from 531 to 541. He rose from a clerk's post and was known for raising money without mercy.
